subject: Opaque-path diagnostics and cost-tracing for per-route tiles

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: sanjay.rao@acme.com

Subject: Opaque-path diagnostics + cost-tracing for per-route tiles

Team —

Quick product ask from the Acme pilot: they want a single place in Console where an SRE or product manager can see:
- "opaque" inference paths (calls that hit multiple route variants / fallbacks) and the fraction of tokens attributable to those paths
- per-path cost and p95 latency (so we can tie tail latency to increased token spend)
- a way to filter by tenant, route, and time window and to export the sampled traces for billing reconciliation

Attached: a small sample export from Acme showing opaque-path ids and counts. The ask is scoped as a Console tile + export endpoint — not a full obs overhaul.

Questions I have for engineering/analytics:
1) feasible to expose per-path cost attribution at the tile level without exploding cardinality?
2) sampling guidance (how much to sample and how to surface that to customers)
3) any immediate SLA or billing implications we should flag to Acme before we demo?

Can you reply with a short plan + risks by EOD tomorrow? Sanjay (cc) is watching — trying to avoid another surprise in the renewal conversation.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Product Manager, Console + Observability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: opaque-paths-sample.csv (csv)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Opaque-path diagnostics + cost-tracing for per-route tiles

Lauren —

Brief response / feasibility notes:
- We can surface per-path token counts and p95 latency if we maintain a sampled KV cache of path signatures (path signature = sequence of route variants + fallback reasons). However, cardinality can blow up for chat-heavy tenants that use function calling + tools.
- Proposal: implement continuous sampling with two retention modes — "high-fidelity" (10% of requests) for enterprise tenants on Dedicated, and "economy" (0.5-1%) for hosted by default. Sampling fractions configurable per-tenant.
- Cost attribution: we can compute per-path token spend as (tokens_generated * model_unit_cost) per sampled trace and extrapolate to total traffic using sample weights. It's an estimator and will have an error margin that depends on sampling rate.
- Instrumentation effort: ~2 sprint points to add path signature logging + sampling knobs to runtime, ~3 points to add an incremental aggregator that feeds a metrics table. Frontend tile + export UI another 3 points.

Risks:
- Sampling low will underreport rare expensive fallbacks.
- For Dedication customers with bursty usage, we'll need a fallback tracing mode to avoid losing SLOs when we increase sampling.

I'll put a short RFC into OBS-731 with the data model and an example of the path signature format.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal SW Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Lauren / team —

I sketched a couple of dashboards and attached a quick mock (per-route-tile-mock.png). Suggested panels:
1) Top opaque path signatures by spend (last 24h / 7d) — table with sample count, estimated total tokens, extrapolated spend, p95 latency.
2) Heatmap: route -> fallback reason -> estimated cost ratio (helps spot bad fallbacks).
3) Trace export panel: show sampling rate, sample weight, and an export link that dumps sampled traces to Drive/CSV for finance reconciliation.
4) Error / anomaly flag: signal any path whose extrapolated spend grows >20% week-over-week — mark as "investigate".

Notes:
- We should record sampling_rate as metadata in the tile UI so customers understand the estimator.
- For the export, include a column with the sample_weight so finance can re-weight values.

I've added OBS-731 comments with the mock and a small SQL sketch for the aggregator (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OBS-731). If we agree on the sampling defaults Marcus suggested, I can prototype the aggregator queries in the next analytics sprint.

Grace O'Connor
Product Analytics
Redwood Inference

Quick ops note —

If we expose estimated spend and sampling-weighted exports to customers, we need an ops playbook that covers:
- When a tile shows a sudden spike caused by an internal fallback, the tile should link to the SLO-fallback runbook and provide a one-click "request emergency rollback" (this is a UX ask for Console).
- For Dedicated customers, sampling rate increases for debugging must be gated by quota checks — we don't want a support debug to trigger expensive model usage.
- We should add a brief legal-friendly disclaimer in the export about estimator error margins; finance may use it for reconciliation only after agreeing to a calibration run.

I'll draft the runbook and a small quota-check API by EOD Friday if folks want me to own it.

— Logan
Logan Wright
SRE Lead, Inference Operations
Redwood Inference
